title: Municipalities: Beware of Changes in Flock’s Legal Terms if You’re Using or Considering License Plate Readers | ACLU
summary: The ACLU warns municipalities that Flock Safety has made several changes to its standard terms and conditions that shift power from customer agencies to the company, including removing a prohibition on selling customer data, granting Flock control over data access, creating a perpetual license to use customer data, and expanding liability protections and arbitration requirements. The piece urges cities to consult counsel before signing or renewing Flock contracts.

key_quotes.quote: Flock's previous T&C stated flatly, "Flock does not own and shall not sell Customer Data." That language is now absent from their T&C.

The T&C now add a "perpetual" right for Flock to use customer data to "support and improve" its services — allowing the company to keep using driver surveillance data even after a town, city, or other customer has terminated its relationship with Flock

makes it harder for customers to terminate Flock contracts, including when a town or city council votes not to approve a contract or fails to appropriate the funds for it, as nearly 50 cities have done in the past year alone
